title: Before the Shutters
stanzas: At five the street is still a rumor of itself.
A tailgate drops. Crates come down hand to hand,
each with a wet corner and the smell of cabbage.
The fish man hoses his board twice,
lays out silver on salt-scrubbed wood,
and turns the ice until it goes translucent.
Nobody talks much yet. The scale sits level,
brass weights cold in the palm, heavier
than their size has any right to be.
Then the shutters go up, one after another,
and the price of tomatoes climbs before the sun
has cleared the roof of the bus stand.
I buy two lemons for the smell on my fingers
and take the long way home through fish air,
carrying the morning in a paper bag.
